two_origin_design: Change the existing concrete CrossOriginPeer alias to ConnectionPeer<TestResult<Vec<String>>> and guard each original task immediately at its canonical spawn. Keep both original worker bodies and observation seams unchanged.
Keep the successful caller resource carrier alive until both joins and original header assertions complete; retain the original caller error by move.
If caller failed, record cancellation separately for each unfinished original peer and abort both before the first await.

Poll the two original borrowed join handles concurrently under their own finite collection deadlines. A completed failure on either side must trigger cancellation of every other unfinished peer before further cleanup awaits. A sequential origin-first join alone does not promptly cover a destination fault while origin is Pending.

Retain successful head vectors and flatten original task outcomes exactly once. Aggregate errors in stable origin-then-destination order regardless of completion order; caller remains primary and the worker-pair aggregate is cleanup. Reuse existing FixtureFailures, with no new shared framework.

A join deadline keeps its original Elapsed. Abort the timed-out original task and attempt a finite cancellation join; also cancel the other pending original task before that attempt. Preserve additional actual cleanup errors, and never treat original timeout as success.
Accept JoinError cancellation only after a recorded local abort request for that same unfinished original handle. Completed serving I/O, unrelated JoinError and panic remain errors.
Drop is an abort safeguard for the original pair, not an asynchronous join or every-result guarantee. Outer caller deadlines must not encompass the explicit cleanup phase.

remaining_design: Apply immediate existing concrete guard to each of the nine actual original tasks, retaining original result types. Capture caller result without early propagation, keep its successful resources alive, then collect the original peer outside the caller operation bound and compose both outcomes. Share a factory only where multiple compatible ordinary callers already exist. Do not route distinct TLS/plaintext/time-domain workers through a broad mode framework.
